run.executedVia: Playwright runner, no browser: ServiceNow read over cnit and the Scripted REST API as sf.integration, Salesforce read over the sf CLI and anonymous Apex against the deployed classes. Every case reads both sides.

case.title: Named credential and Client Credentials auth

steps.text: List the named credentials in the org.
Confirm every Apex reference uses that exact name.
Confirm no credential has been committed to source.
Read the ServiceNow-side integration properties and their storage types.
Confirm the sync script requests a token by Client Credentials rather than JWT.

observations: Deviation to record in the TDD delta: Client Credentials rather than JWT bearer, because ServiceNow's jwt_provider table has no iss/sub/aud fields. JWT remains the better production answer.
The named credential is created by hand and deliberately not in source: Salesforce will not deploy one without a password, and that password must not sit in a client-facing directory.
expected: The named credential is called ServiceNow_CAF exactly.
No credential has leaked into force-app/namedCredentials/.
The client secret property is encrypted (password2).
Inbound authenticates as sf.integration; outbound obtains a token via Client Credentials.
actual: Named credential present: ServiceNow_CAF, endpoint https://dev281754.service-now.com, principal NamedUser
Files in force-app/namedCredentials/: the directory does not exist
Client secret property: x_gskn2_caf_compli.sf.client_secret, type = password2
Outbound grant type in CAFSalesforceSync: client_credentials
case.verdictReason: Named credential, Apex references, source hygiene and secret storage all as specified.
